title: The Potential of Exercise Programs and Self-Management for Breast Cancer Patients with Secondary Lymphedema
summary: Background: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women and leads to breast cancer-related secondary lymphedema (BCRL) in approximately 20% of patients within the first two years following diagnosis or treatment. BCRL is a chronic condition characterized by swelling in one or both arms. Symptoms include pain, a feeling of heaviness and tightness, as well as functional limitations and psychosocial impairments. The guideline-recommended treatment for BCRL is complex decongestive therapy (CDT), which consists of four components (skin care, compression, self-exercises, and manual lymphatic drainage (MLD)). The first three components, in particular, are the responsibility of the patients and are thus part of self-management. To what extent the promotion of self-management—and specifically the performance of self-exercises—is adequately addressed in outpatient care in Germany remains a knowledge gap. Research Question: The project addresses the question of to what extent self-exercises and the promotion of self-management among patients are addressed in the care of lymphedema in Germany. Methodology: Analysis of routine data from statutory health insurance, quantitative online surveys of patients and physical therapists, and workshops to formulate recommendations for action.
conditions: Lymphedema of the upper and lower extremities, Stage I

interventions.name: Analysis of prescribing and care practices for breast-cancer related lympedema (BCRL), as well as a health economic assessment based on routine data from statutory health insurance.
Assessment of clinical practice for BCRL through surveys of patients and physical therapists.
Workshops to identify recommendations for action, involving relevant stakeholders.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients: Primary diagnosis: ICD-C50.x: Malignant neoplasm of the breast [mammary gland] or enrollment in the DMP Breast Cancer program; more than 3 months ago AND at least one of the following ICD diagnosis codes for coding lymphedema: - I97.20 – I97.22 Lymphedema following (partial) mastectomy (with lymphadenectomy), Stage I–III - I97.29 Lymphedema following (partial) mastectomy (with lymphadenectomy), unspecified - I89.00 – I89.02 Lymphedema of the upper and lower extremity(ies), Stage I–III - I89.09 Lymphedema, unspecified Two target populations are distinguished: Target population A: Patients with a prescription for a therapeutic agent related to the indication within the last 3 months Target population B: Patients without a prescription for a therapeutic agent related to the indication within the last 12 months
Physical therapists: Treatment experience with breast cancer patients covered by statutory health insurance who have secondary lymphedema and who work in the outpatient sector
Exclusion criteria:
Patients: Surgical treatment for breast cancer within the last 3 months (OPS: 8-54, 8-87) - Ongoing oncological therapy (OPS: -, 8-52, 8-53.-, 8-54) - Breast reconstruction within the last 6 weeks (OPS: 5-885.-, 5-886.-) - Presence of secondary malignant neoplasm (recurrence) (ICD: C77.x, C79.x) - Palliative care (EBM code: 03370 – 03373 or “Prescription for specialized outpatient palliative care” [SAPV]) - Cognitive impairments beyond mild cognitive impairment (MCI) (ICD: U51.1, U51.2, F00.x, F01.x, F02.x, F03, F05.x).
Physical therapists: None
